Plains are one of the major landforms on Earth, characterized by vast, relatively flat or gently rolling stretches of land with low relief. They cover more than one-third of the planet's land area and can be found on every continent. These expansive landscapes are formed through various geological processes, such as the deposition of sediment by rivers, the erosion of hills and mountains over millions of years, or even the cooling of widespread lava flows. Because they lack significant structural barriers like high mountains or deep valleys, plains offer uninterrupted horizons that uniquely shape local climates and weather patterns.
Depending on their location and formation, plains are generally categorized into three main types: coastal, alluvial, and inland plains. Coastal plains lie adjacent to an ocean and are often formed by the accumulation of marine sediments or the gradual drop of sea levels. Alluvial plains, on the other hand, are created by rivers that flood their banks and deposit rich layers of silt, sand, and clay over time. Inland plains, such as the Great Plains of North America, are situated deep within continents, often shaped by ancient glacial movements or wind-driven erosion that leveled the terrain over vast eras.
Due to their unique geography, plains often feature some of the most fertile soils on earth, making them global hubs for agriculture. Alluvial plains, in particular, are packed with organic nutrients refreshed by periodic river floods. This deep, rich soil, combined with flat terrain that accommodates large-scale farming machinery, allows plains to serve as the world's primary breadbaskets. Vast expanses of wheat, corn, rice, and soy dominate these regions, supporting global food supplies and driving massive agricultural economies.
Beyond crop cultivation, plains support distinct and diverse ecosystems that have adapted to open environments. Grasslands, savannas, and prairies are the most common natural habitats found on plains, hosting a wide array of wildlife. In the absence of dense forest cover, animals living on plains have evolved specialized survival traits. Large herbivores, such as bison in North America or zebras and wildebeests in the African Serengeti, rely on speed, keen eyesight, and herd behavior to protect themselves from predators across the wide-open spaces.
Throughout human history, plains have been the cradle of major civilizations and remain centers of high population density today. The flat topography makes it exceptionally easy to build roads, railways, and sprawling cities without the engineering challenges posed by mountainous terrain. Major urban centers and historical empires originally flourished along river plains—such as the Nile River Valley or the Indo-Gangetic Plain—because the land provided an ideal combination of reliable freshwater, easy transport routes, and abundant food production.

Start by preheating your oven to 350°F or 175°C and actually wait until it fully reaches that temperature because ovens love to lie about being ready and if you rush it your brownies will bake the mixture becomes glossy and thickened and slightly grainy which might look unimportant but is actually one of the biggest contributors to that shiny, crinkly, paper-thin crust on top that people dessert and that’s your first sign you’re on the right track even though you are still several steps away from actual brownies, then crack in 2 large room-temperature eggs one at a time and mix very well after each addition making sure the batter becomes smooth and cohesive and if you want to go the extra mile you can whisk the mixture for a solid minute or two which incorporates a bit of air and helps dissolve the sugar further and contributes even more to that glossy top layer so now you’re basically stacking small advantages in your favor like some kind of brownie strategist, then add in 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract and stir it in even though it feels like a tiny amount because skipping it would leave your brownies tasting slightly flat and one-dimensional which is not what we’re aiming for in this unnecessarily detailed but extremely effective process, then move on to the dry ingredients by adding 1/2 cup or 45 grams of unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 cup or 65 grams of all-purpose flour, and 1/4 teaspoon of salt and begin mixing slowly and carefully until everything is just combined because overmixing at this stage develops the gluten in the flour and can turn your brownies from soft and fudgy into something tougher and more cake-like which might be what you want but probably isn’t if you’ve made it this far into a ridiculously long brownie sentence, and as the batter thickens you’ll notice it becomes rich and dark and harder to stir which is completely normal and actually a good sign that your ratios are correct, then at this point you can fold in any extras you want such as chocolate chips for melted pockets of chocolate, chunks of a chocolate bar for uneven gooey bites, chopped nuts for crunch, swirls of peanut butter or Nutella for a marbled effect, or even something chaotic like crushed cookies if you feel like pushing the limits of what a brownie can be, then prepare an 8x8 inch baking pan by lining it with parchment paper making sure there’s a bit of overhang on the sides so you can lift the brownies out later without having to perform some kind of risky knife operation that could destroy the edges, and once your pan is ready pour the batter into it and spread it evenly into all corners using a spatula or the back of a spoon because uneven batter distribution leads to uneven baking and we’ve already come too far to let that happen now, then gently tap the pan on the counter a couple of times to release any large air bubbles which helps create a more consistent texture throughout instead of random holes appearing like your brownies have been aerated for no reason, and now place the pan into your fully preheated oven and bake for around 20 to 25 minutes while resisting the incredibly strong urge to open the oven door repeatedly to check on them because every time you do that you drop the temperature and interfere with the baking process and essentially sabotage your own effort, and as they bake your kitchen will start to smell like chocolate in a way that makes waiting feel unnecessarily difficult but patience here is part of the process whether you like it or not, and when you reach around the 20-minute mark you can begin checking for doneness by inserting a toothpick into the center where if it comes out with wet batter it clearly needs more time, if it comes out with a few moist crumbs clinging to it then you’ve hit the ideal fudgy brownie zone, and if it comes out completely clean then your brownies are more on the cakey side and slightly overbaked for a fudgy preference but still completely edible so it’s not the end of the world, then once done remove the pan from the oven and place it on a heat-safe surface and now comes one of the most overlooked but absolutely critical steps which is letting the brownies cool in the pan for at least 30 minutes because during this time they continue to set and firm up and if you cut into them too early they will fall apart and you’ll end up with a pile of delicious but structurally questionable chocolate pieces instead of clean slices, and while you’re waiting you might question whether the wait is worth it but it is because the texture improves significantly as they cool, and once they have cooled enough use the parchment paper overhang to lift the entire slab out of the pan and place it on a cutting board and slice it into squares Unsalted butter: ½ cup (115g), cubed
Whole milk: 1 cup (240ml)
Baking powder: 2 ½ tsp
Vanilla extract: 3 tsp
Vegetable oil: 3 tsp (secret for extra moisture)
Salt: ¼ tsp 
RecipeTin Eats
RecipeTin Eats
Instructions
Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Grease and line two 8-inch round cake pans with parchment paper.
Aerating Eggs: Beat eggs for 30 seconds. Slowly add sugar and continue beating on high for about 7 minutes until the mixture triples in volume and turns white.
Mixing Flour: Gently whisk in the flour, baking powder, and salt in three batches on the lowest speed just until combined. Do not overmix.
Hot Milk Mixture: Heat milk and butter together (microwave or stove) until the butter is just melted. Stir in the vanilla and oil.
Combine: Take about 1 cup of the egg batter and whisk it into the hot milk to lighten it. Then, slowly pour this mixture back into the main batter while mixing on low.
Bake: Pour into pans and bake for 30 minutes. A toothpick should come out clean.

cool but heres the fnaf lore The story begins in 1983 with the opening of Fredbear's Family Diner, a family restaurant founded by William Afton and Henry Emily. The diner featured spring-lock animatronics, which could function as both autonomous robots and wearable suits. However, these suits were dangerous, as moisture or sudden movement could cause the internal mechanisms to snap shut on the wearer.
Tragedy strikes Henry's family first. His daughter, Charlotte Emily (Charlie), is murdered outside one of their establishments by William Afton. Her soul goes on to possess the Puppet animatronic.
The most infamous event of this era is the Bite of '83. William Afton's youngest son, the Crying Child (often referred to as CC), is terrified of the animatronics. His older brother, Michael Afton, and his friends, as a cruel prank, force the Crying Child into Fredbear's mouth during a birthday party. The animatronic's jaw clamps down, crushing the child's head and causing a fatal injury. The Crying Child's spirit is believed by many theorists to possess Golden FreddyFollowing the diner's closure, Fazbear Entertainment attempts to continue the franchise, leading to new pizzerias. In an unknown year (often theorized to be 1985), William Afton lures five more children into a back room of a Freddy Fazbear's Pizza location and murders them. The victims — Gabriel, Jeremy, Susie, Fritz, and Cassidy — have their bodies hidden inside the main four animatronics: Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, and Foxy. This causes the animatronics to emit a foul odor and leak blood and mucus, leading to health department sanctions and the eventual decline of the restaurant. The children's souls now possess these characters, seeking vengeance.Michael Afton, William's other son, is a central figure throughout the games. William, obsessed with immortality and the supernatural "remnant" (a substance linked to the souls of the dead), sends Michael to his underground facility, Circus Baby's Entertainment and Rental (the setting of Sister Location). This location houses advanced "Funtime" animatronics designed by William to capture children.
Michael is working to find his sister, Elizabeth Afton, whose soul possesses the main animatronic, Circus Baby, after being accidentally killed by the robot years earlier. At the end of Sister Location, all the Funtime animatronics merge into a single entity called Ennard, which scoops Michael and uses his body as a disguise to escape the facility. Michael's body decays until Ennard leaves him, but Michael is miraculously reanimated, driven to find his father and "put him back together"Years later, Henry Emily, determined to end William's reign of terror, designs a fake pizzeria in Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator (FNaF 6) as a trap. He lures all the remaining possessed animatronics and William Afton (now known as Springtrap, having been spring-locked inside a Spring Bonnie suit years prior while hiding from the spirits of his victims) to the location.
Henry initiates a controlled fire, burning the building to the ground in an attempt to free the trapped souls and end William Afton's life once and for all. Henry's plan works for most of the souls, who find peace in the "Happiest Day" minigame.The story continues in the age of virtual reality with FNaF Help Wanted. Fazbear Entertainment attempts to sanitize their reputation by making a VR game based on the "urban legends" of the pizzerias. During the development, a circuit board from the burned-down Springtrap suit is scanned into the game, introducing a digital version of William Afton's consciousness, known as Glitchtrap. Glitchtrap attempts to control a beta tester named Vanessa (or Vanny), who becomes his loyal follower.
The modern storyline, including Security Breach and Help Wanted 2, introduces the Mimic, a new antagonist that complicates the lore. William Afton's influence persists through this digital virus and his followers, continuing the cycle of fear and possession that defines the Five Nights at Freddy's universe.

The Lockheed Martin/Boeing F-22 Raptor is an American twin-engine, all-weather, supersonic stealth fighter aircraft. As a product of the United States Air Force's Advanced Tactical Fighter (ATF) program, the aircraft was designed as an air superiority fighter, but also incorporates ground attack, electronic warfare, and signals intelligence capabilities. The prime contractor, Lockheed Martin, built most of the F-22 airframe and weapons systems and conducted final assembly, while program partner Boeing provided the wings, aft fuselage, avionics integration, and training systems.

First flown in 1997, the F-22 descended from the Lockheed YF-22 and was variously designated F-22 and F/A-22 before it formally entered service in December 2005 as the F-22A. Although the U.S. Air Force (USAF) had originally planned to buy a total of 750 ATFs to replace its F-15 Eagles, it later scaled down to 381, and the program was ultimately cut to 195 aircraft — 187 of them operational models — in 2009 due to political opposition from high costs, a lack of air-to-air missions at the time of production, and the development of the more affordable and versatile F-35.[N 2] The last aircraft was delivered in 2012.

The F-22 is a critical component of the USAF's current high-end tactical airpower. While it had a protracted development and initial operational difficulties, the aircraft became the service's leading platform for air-to-air missions against peer adversaries. Although designed for counter-air operations, the F-22 has also performed strike and electronic surveillance, including missions in the Middle East against the Islamic State and Assad-aligned forces. The F-22 is planned to remain a cornerstone of the USAF's fighter fleet until its succession by the crewed Next Generation Air Dominance fighter.

The first F-22 crash occurred during takeoff at Nellis AFB on 20 December 2004, in which the pilot ejected safely before impact.[293] The investigation revealed that a brief interruption in power during an engine shutdown prior to flight caused a flight-control system malfunction;[294] consequently the aircraft design was corrected to avoid the problem. Following a brief grounding, F-22 operations resumed after a review.[295]

On 25 March 2009, an EMD F-22 crashed 35 miles (56 km) northeast of Edwards AFB during a test flight, resulting in the death of Lockheed Martin test pilot David P. Cooley. An Air Force Materiel Command investigation found that Cooley momentarily lost consciousness during a high-G maneuver, or g-LOC, then ejected when he found himself too low to recover. Cooley was killed during ejection by blunt-force trauma from windblast due to the aircraft's speed. The investigation found no design issues.[296][297]

On 16 November 2010, an F-22 from Elmendorf AFB crashed, killing the pilot, Captain Jeffrey Haney. F-22s were restricted to flying below 25,000 feet, then grounded during the investigation.[298] The crash was attributed to a bleed air system malfunction after an engine overheat condition was detected, shutting down the Environmental Control System (ECS) and OBOGS. The accident review board ruled Haney was to blame, as he did not react properly to engage the emergency oxygen system.[299] Haney's widow sued Lockheed Martin, claiming equipment defects, and later reached a settlement.[300][231] After the ruling, the emergency oxygen system engagement handle was redesigned and the entire system was eventually replaced by an automatic backup.[301][302] On 11 February 2013, the DoD's Inspector General released a report stating that the USAF had erred in blaming Haney, and that facts did not sufficiently support conclusions; the USAF stated that it stood by the ruling.[303]

On 15 November 2012, an F-22 crashed to the east of Tyndall AFB during a training mission. The pilot ejected safely and no injuries were reported on the ground.[304] The investigation determined that a "chafed" electrical wire ignited the fluid in a hydraulic line, causing a fire that damaged the flight controls.[305]

On 15 May 2020, an F-22 from Eglin Air Force Base crashed during a routine training mission shortly after takeoff; the pilot ejected safely. The cause of the crash was attributed to a maintenance error after an aircraft wash resulting in faulty air data sensor readings.[306]
